metadata.name: more
metadata.displayName: more - Display text one screen at a time
metadata.description: Display text one screen at a time

installation.note: more is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The more command displays text files one screen at a time, allowing you to scroll through content page by page. It's an older pager utility, largely superseded by 'less' which offers more features, but more is still widely available and useful for basic text viewing.
when_to_use: View large text files page by page
Read log files without opening an editor
Display command output that might be long
View file contents in a controlled manner

syntax.description: If no file is specified, more reads from standard input. You can navigate using spacebar (next page), Enter (next line), or 'q' (quit).

misconceptions.title: More vs Less
misconceptions.misconception: more and less are the same
misconceptions.reality: less is more advanced - it allows backward navigation, searching, and has more features. 'less' is more, 'more' is less.
misconceptions.tip: Prefer 'less' for most use cases, but 'more' is simpler and available everywhere

misconceptions.title: Editing capability
misconceptions.reality: more is read-only. It only displays files, it cannot modify them.
misconceptions.tip: Use text editors like nano, vim, or gedit to edit files

common_pitfalls.description: more only allows forward navigation, not backward
common_pitfalls.solution: Use 'less' instead if you need to scroll backward through a file

common_pitfalls.description: more may display binary files incorrectly
common_pitfalls.solution: Use 'file' command first to check file type, or use 'hexdump' or 'od' for binary files

related_commands.description: less is a more advanced pager with backward navigation and search capabilities
cat displays entire file at once, while more displays page by page
head shows first lines, more shows entire file page by page
tail shows last lines, more shows entire file page by page

best_practices: Use 'less' instead of 'more' for better navigation features
Press 'q' to quit, not Ctrl+C (which may leave terminal in alternate screen mode)
Use spacebar for next page, Enter for next line
Combine with pipes to view long command output
performance_tips: For very large files, 'less' is more efficient
Using '+number' to jump to a line is faster than scrolling
